title: Dimissioni a riad dopo l'eliminazione dal mondiale
titles: DIMISSIONI A RIAD DOPO L'ELIMINAZIONE DAL MONDIALE
DIMISSIONI A RIAD DOPO L'ELIMINAZIONE DAL MONDIALE
DIMISSIONI A RIAD DOPO L'ELIMINAZIONE DAL MONDIALE
occhiello: DIMISSIONI A RIAD DOPO L'ELIMINAZIONE DAL MONDIALE
lead: Riad, 29 giugno 2026. L'eliminazione precoce della Nazionale Saudita dal torneo Mondiale segna la fine dell'era di Yasser Al-Misehal ai vertici della Federcalcio locale. Il dirigente ha rassegnato le proprie dimissioni con effetto immediato, formalizzando l'addio dopo il fallimento sportivo della selezione Nazionale. La decisione giunge al culmine di una competizione che aveva caricato il movimento calcistico del Paese di aspettative altissime, rivelatesi incompatibili con l'esito del campo.
corpo1: Secondo quanto riportato dall'agenzia ANSA, la notizia delle dimissioni di Yasser Al-Misehal è stata ufficializzata nelle ore successive alla sconfitta che ha sancito l'esclusione definitiva dell'Arabia Saudita dalla rassegna iridata. Il dirigente, figura Centrale nell'Organizzazione sportiva del Regno, lascia la guida della Federcalcio dopo un periodo caratterizzato da investimenti massicci e da una proiezione Internazionale senza precedenti. Il ruolo di Al-Misehal era stato determinante non solo nella gestione della Nazionale, ma soprattutto nelle dinamiche di diplomazia sportiva che hanno portato all'assegnazione della Coppa del Mondo 2034. Il suo addio, sebbene presentato come una conseguenza diretta della mancata qualificazione agli ottavi di finale, chiude una fase di gestione in cui il Calcio è stato utilizzato come principale asset di soft power Saudita. La Federcalcio ha confermato la ricezione delle dimissioni, annunciando l'avvio di una fase di transizione interna mirata a riorganizzare i vertici societari e la struttura tecnica del movimento. Non sono stati ancora resi noti i nomi dei potenziali successori, ma l'ambiente federale appare in una condizione di profonda revisione strategica. La sconfitta sul terreno di gioco, interpretata dai vertici come un inaccettabile passo falso per il prestigio Nazionale, ha accelerato un processo di defenestrazione che coinvolge ora anche lo staff tecnico della squadra, la cui posizione risulta compromessa in seguito ai risultati deludenti ottenuti nel girone eliminatorio.

        *   Current news: Al-Misehal resigned after the loss/elimination.
        *   Context: Massive investments, soft power, hosting 2034 World Cup.
           Scenario: Scenario 3 (Crisis and Locker Room/Management) or Scenario 4 (Finance/Governance). Since the prompt focuses on the consequences and the reason* behind the resignation (economic/strategic), I should lean into the economic/strategic fallout.

The summary is just a repeat of the lead. There are no new* specific facts in the provided text (no specific numbers for severance, no specific names of successors, no specific dollar amounts for the loss of prestige/revenue).

        *   Word count: 350-400 words.
        *   Content: Deepen context or add developments (since no new developments are in the source, I must deepen the existing context using the persona's expertise).
        *   Tone: Analytical, economic focus, no "heroic" language, no "miracles", use names (Al-Misehal).
           Structure: Avoid repeating Corpo 1. Focus on the why and the economic/strategic cost*.
        *   Closing: Net statement anchored in concrete fact.
        *   Constraint: No questions, no generic formulas, no explicit moralizing.

       What is the real cost here?* It's not just a loss in a match; it's a failure of a massive investment in soft power.
       The 2034 World Cup context:* The investment in the 2034 bid and the infrastructure is billions. A failure in 2026 undermines the "proof of concept" for the Saudi sports project.
       The "Why":* Al-Misehal wasn't just a football guy; he was a diplomat/manager. His failure is a failure of the ROI (Return on Investment) on the national team's performance.
       The "Who":* The decision likely comes from the higher powers (Vision 2030/PIF/Crown Prince's circle), not just a board of directors.
       The "What":* The cost of the transition. The restructuring of the Federation.

       Drafting thought 1 (The Economic Angle):* The resignation isn't just about a scoreline. It's about the mismatch between the billions spent on player acquisitions and the actual performance. If the goal was to use the 2026 World Cup as a showcase for the Saudi footballing evolution, the failure is a strategic setback.

       Drafting thought 2 (The Soft Power Angle):* The 2034 World Cup is the ultimate goal. The 2026 failure creates a narrative gap. Investors and sponsors look at performance metrics.

       Refining the Tone (Matteo Galli style):* Use terms like "asset," "ritorno sull'investimento," "progetto di soft power." Avoid "tragedy" or "disaster." Use "inefficienza" or "scostamento dai target."

       Integrating the "Data/Logic" requirement: Since I don't have specific numbers in the source (as per the instruction "don't invent"), I will focus on the logic* of the investment. The failure is the divergence between the capital injected into the league/national team and the competitive output.

       Wait, I need to be careful:* The prompt says "don't invent names/figures/declarations absent from the source."
       Source says:* "investimenti massicci," "proiezione Internazionale," "assegnazione della Coppa del Mondo 2034," "transizione interna."
       I can expand on:* The relationship between the 2026 result and the 2034 objective. The concept of "soft power" as a business asset. The cost of the "transizione" (implied as a restructuring of costs).

       Opening:* Move away from the match result (already in Corpo 1) and move toward the strategic implications. The resignation of Al-Misehal is a correction of a management model that failed to convert financial liquidity into sporting results.
       Middle: Discuss the 2034 World Cup. The 2026 failure isn't just a sporting exit; it's a failure to validate the "Saudi Model" before the 2034 cycle begins. The gap between the massive capital influx and the team's actual performance metrics (expected goals, defensive stability, etc. - Though I shouldn't invent specific stats, I can talk about the gap*).
       Closing:* The transition period will likely focus on a more technocratic management to safeguard the 2034 roadmap.

       Word count check:* I need to reach ~350 words.
       Constraint check:* No "fenomenale," no "eroica." No "miracolo."
       Tone check:* Is it "analitico-appassionato"? Yes.

    Self-Correction during drafting: I must avoid saying "The cost of the resignation is X million" because I don't have that number in the source. I will instead focus on the strategic cost and the recalibration of the investment model.

    Drafting Content:
    The departure of Al-Misehal represents the first significant rupture in the "Vision 2030" sports strategy. The goal was to use the national team as a flagship for the massive capital transfers seen in the domestic league. However, the performance in 2026 shows a disconnect between the financial weight of the federation and its competitive efficiency. This isn't a mere personnel change; it's a recalibration of the soft power asset. The 2034 World Cup requires a stable institutional framework. The "transition" mentioned by the federation will likely involve a shift from a diplomatic management style to one focused on technical performance metrics to avoid further erosion of the brand value associated with Saudi football.

    Expanding to meet length:
    Talk about the "return on investment" of the diplomatic efforts. The 2034 bid was a long-term asset
